questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 38 deals with When right of private defence of body extends to causing death. It sits in Chapter III — General Exceptions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Private defence of body extends to causing death in listed situations: a reasonably apprehended assault that may cause death, grievous hurt, rape, gratifying unnatural lust, kidnapping/abducting, or throwing/attempting acid.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 38 is the rule on “When right of private defence of body extends to causing death”. The section provides that the right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions specified in section 37, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the assailant, if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right be of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. The right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions specified in section 37, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the assailant, if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right be of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:—
2. (a) such an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that death will otherwise be the consequence of such assault;
3. (b) such an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence of such assault;
4. (c) an assault with the intention of committing rape;
5. (d) an assault with the intention of gratifying unnatural lust;
6. (e) an assault with the intention of kidnapping or abducting;
7. (f) an assault with the intention of wrongfully confining a person, under circumstances which may reasonably cause him to apprehend that he will be unable to have recourse to the public authorities for his release;
8. (g) an act of throwing or administering acid or an attempt to throw or administer acid which may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence of such act

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 38. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 34, BNS s. 101. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 38 is the complete current-law heading for When right of private defence of body extends to causing death. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. When an act is not an offence: mistake, accident, infancy, unsoundness, consent, compulsion — and the right of private defence.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Distinction. Contrast BNS s. 38 with BNS s. 34, BNS s. 101. Write a short table in prose: meaning, ingredients, stage of the case, consequence. Confusion of neighbouring sections is the most common reason arguments collapse under judicial scrutiny.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 38.”

learningObjectives: Master the seven specific circumstances under BNS s. 38 where private defence of the body extends to causing death.
Analyze the requirement of reasonable apprehension of death, grievous hurt, rape, unnatural lust, abduction, confinement, or acid attack.
Apply the restrictions of s. 37 to lethal self-defence.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 38 provides that the right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions mentioned in section 37, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the assailant, if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right be of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated: (First) — Such an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that death will otherwise be the consequence; (Secondly) — Such an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence; (Thirdly) — An assault with the intention of committing rape; (Fourthly) — An assault with the intention of gratifying unnatural lust; (Fifthly) — An assault with the intention of kidnapping or abducting; (Sixthly) — An assault with the intention of wrongfully confining a person, under circumstances which may reasonably cause him to apprehend that he will be unable to have recourse to the public authorities for his release; (Seventhly) — An act of throwing or administering acid or an attempt to throw or administer acid which may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Where an unlawful assault threatens supreme bodily violations — death, grievous hurt, rape, unnatural lust, kidnapping, inescapable confinement, or acid attacks — the law permits the victim or rescuer to voluntarily cause the death of the assailant to preserve life, bodily integrity, and liberty.
statutoryFramework: Chapter III — General Exceptions, BNS s. 38 (corresponding to IPC s. 100).
Operational prerequisite: Subject to s. 37 restrictions (proportionality, absence of recourse).
3. Assault with intention of committing rape.
4. Assault with intention of gratifying unnatural lust.
5. Assault with intention of kidnapping or abducting.
6. Assault with intention of wrongful confinement with no recourse to public authorities.
7. Act or attempt of throwing/administering acid causing apprehension of grievous hurt.
essentialIngredients: The victim faced an assault falling under one of the seven enumerated categories.
The assault reasonably generated apprehension of the specified grave peril.
The lethal force was inflicted during the subsistence of the apprehension.
The force conformed to the negative restrictions in s. 37.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 38 is the most critical provision in the law of homicide and self-defence. Taking a human life is justified only when the threat reaches the highest gravity specified in clauses First through Seventhly. The test is objective based on contemporaneous circumstances: did the accused have a reasonable apprehension of death, grievous hurt, rape, or acid violence? The law does not expect an assaulted victim to weigh their blows in 'golden scales'. If an attacker charges with a raised battleaxe or firearm, the defender is not obliged to wait until he is struck; he may shoot or strike lethally immediately.
examples: Teaching example (Apprehension of grievous hurt): An attacker pins a woman to the ground and raises an iron rod to shatter her skull. She grabs a nearby kitchen knife and stabs the attacker in the chest, killing him. Section 38 (First/Secondly) applies; her act is completely justified.

Teaching example (Attempted rape): An assailant corners a woman in an isolated alley, tears her clothes, and attempts to rape her. She strikes him on the temple with a heavy stone, causing fatal injury. Section 38 (Thirdly) protects her.
distinctions: Section 38 vs Section 39: Section 38 applies to the seven grave assaults and extends to causing death; Section 39 applies to all other bodily assaults and permits harm short of death.
Reasonable apprehension vs Realized injury: The right arises upon reasonable apprehension; the victim need not wait to receive a mortal wound before defending lethally.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who shot an assailant advancing with a drawn acid bottle can claim exemption under BNS s. 38.
Rule: Under BNS s. 38 (Seventhly), an attempt to throw or administer acid causing apprehension of grievous hurt justifies causing death in private defence.
Application: Establish that the bottle contained acid, that the assailant was in throwing range and threatening the victim, and that no public authority was at hand.
Conclusion: The lethal defence falls squarely within s. 38 (Seventhly); the accused is entitled to complete acquittal.
